ao_2024_25.title: Amended AO 2024-25 Civil Case Management - Mandatory Review of Civil Cases and Entry of Case Management Orders
ao_2024_25.scope: Circuit-wide civil actions, except actions within a Rule 1.200 exception (paragraph 1).
key_requirements: For cases subject to the order, the presiding judge assigns a case-management track within 120 days of commencement; complex cases proceed under Rule 1.201.
Plaintiff or counsel files the Notice of Final Service within five days of service on the last-named defendant and serves the assigned judicial assistant; clerk filing alone is insufficient.
A stipulated amended case-management order must meet the stated time/form requirements and be submitted for final approval by the presiding judge; stipulation alone does not amend the order.
ao_2024_25.review_scope: General applicability and office routing in paragraphs 1–7; stated effective/issuance dates retained. No case-specific deadline calculation or exhaustive motion analysis.

srcad_2019_03.title: SRCAD 2019-03 Submission and Distribution Requirements for Orders in Civil Proceedings
srcad_2019_03.scope: Directive states applicability to parties in civil, probate and family proceedings in Santa Rosa; practical order-submission rules only.
key_requirements: Attorneys use the Portal Proposed Order function except as otherwise directed by the presiding judge case by case or specified by statute, rule or Supreme Court administrative order.

Attorneys excused under Rule 2.516 may use paper with a certificate of service, conforming copies and addressed stamped envelopes. Unregistered pro se litigants may submit Word by email or paper with copies/envelopes; only paper submissions include a certificate of service.

The directive states specific attorney-service and certificate-of-compliance duties in cases with one pro se party; its required notice qualifies the five-business-day service duty by the pro se party lacking Portal access/registration. See paragraphs 2–3 for wording; do not generalize to every pro se party.
Paragraph 4 states that electronic proposed orders no longer include a certificate of service effective October 1, 2019.
srcad_2019_03.review_scope: Pages 1–2 general submission rules and qualifications; historical distribution list reviewed solely as a lead, not current appointment evidence.
